summary.headline: V-Mart Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 32%, but festive shift kept like-for-like growth at 3% reported.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 18% YoY with reported SSSG of 3%; management said festive-adjusted like-for-like growth was 11%, as Navratri moved into Q3 (Oct 11 vs Sep 22 last year). Gross margin was stable at 33.5% vs 33.6%, and the expense ratio improved slightly on lower employee costs, so EBITDA margin held. Unlimited (South India) EBITDA margin rose to 11.6% from 10.5%, now ahead of V-Mart on a YTD pre-Ind AS basis. Store network reached 613 after 23 openings and 1 closure in the quarter, with short-term borrowings up to INR 190 crore on festive working capital.

segments.name: V-Mart (core format)
segments.commentary: Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin 8.8% in Q2; management expects V-Mart profitability to be strong in Q3, where the bulk of its business falls.

segments.name: Unlimited (South India)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 11.6% vs 10.5% last year; YTD sales per sq ft INR 681, up 15%; now ahead of V-Mart on YTD EBITDA margin pre-Ind AS. Prices kept about 5% higher for similar products.

segments.name: LimeRoad (online)
segments.commentary: Top line up about 55%, losses cut to 8% of revenue from about 18%; 58% of online orders fulfilled from store inventory; digital users up 37%.

guidance_outlook: Management estimates total sales growth of 17% to 20% and will continue with that.
Plans to open at least 90 to 100 stores in FY27; 38 opened in H1 against 2 closures, with about 40 to 42 more expected.
Price increases of 5% to 6% targeted; management said ASP could rise a little more because of mix. Another price increase may be needed in Q4 if crude stays at $110-115.
Expects further inventory days improvement as sales productivity grows; expects more operating efficiency in the coming part of the year.
Festive outlook described as positive but below internal targets; October same-store sales not disclosed.
capex_capacity: Net capex of INR 85 crore in H1 FY27 for new stores, refurbishments, new office in Gurgaon and technology.
Store count 613 across 351 cities after 23 openings in Q2 and 38 in H1; 600-store mark crossed this quarter.
New stores average about 7,500 sq ft (range 7,000 to 8,000 sq ft); new-store area addition about 15% in the last year.
Management said bulk of cash flow will be redeployed into organic store and capacity expansion in the near to medium term.
Intent to focus new openings in South and West India, given Unlimited performance.
demand_pricing: Reported SSSG 3%; festival-adjusted like-for-like growth 11%. Management said the Q2 base was affected by the 19-day festival shift.
Footfalls up 36%; management said the footfall base had anomalies and gave ~35% as the right conversion metric going forward.
Apparel ASP flat YoY in Q2; management expects 5% to 6% price rise, with Q3 mix shifting toward higher ASP items.
Heavy competitive openings: about 150 competitor stores targeting its markets; 70 to 75 locations impacted; intensity highest in East and Central North (Odisha, Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, UP).
Management cited food inflation and geopolitical energy and raw material volatility pressuring value-seeking consumers; 70% of sales from repeat customers; over 45% of customers are Gen Z/Gen Alpha.

qa_highlights.question: Is the business 80% of the way to its portfolio and inventory goal, and when will that show up in SSSG? What about pre-Ind AS margin recovery and gross margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are still below the 2017-19 levels and attributed this to Unlimited and LimeRoad drag and heavy competition. It expects 5% to 6% ASP growth and said margins can absorb about 0.5 percentage points either way. It did not give a bottoming view on gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What was October same-store sales growth and the full-year SSSG expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to report mid-month SSSG. It said the festive outlook was positive but still below targets.

qa_highlights.question: Is consumer spending improving and what is the store addition outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Basket sizes are not growing much; ASP rise is driving value. Management reiterated 17% to 20% sales growth and plans about 40 to 42 more stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store size trend and where is competitive intensity rising, and will price hikes be undercut?
qa_highlights.answer: New stores average about 7,500 sq ft. Competition is most intense in the East and Central North belt. Price rises of 5% to 6% are planned, with ASP possibly rising more.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Unlimited SPSF turnaround and how much further can it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited new product lines, a lower price point, youth and kids wear, and a Gen Z push. It said like-for-like growth beyond double digits would lift SPSF further; no numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will free cash flow be deployed, and what drove the operating cost efficiency and Unlimited margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash flow will go mainly to organic store and capacity expansion. Efficiency came from manpower rationalisation and power analytics, offset by higher minimum wages in UP and Haryana. Unlimited prices are about 5% higher and about 55% of its stores are new with lower rents.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from raw material and crude-linked input costs; Q4 price increase may be needed if crude stays at $110-115 (management said built-in cost up to about $75 crude).
Competitive intensity in East and Central North; about 150 competitor stores opened in target markets.
Working capital: DIO 90 days, short-term borrowings INR 190 crore, vendor payments accelerated by 9 days.
Reported SSSG at 3% versus 11% festival-adjusted; Q3 must show festive recovery.
Rising minimum wages in UP and Haryana raise employee costs; LimeRoad losses still at 8% of revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Unlimited and LimeRoad turnaround and on margin control, but cautious on consumer demand and input costs. Management was evasive on October SSSG and on gross margin trajectory, declining to report mid-month data.
key_quotes: We definitely are seeing a lot of like -for-like momentum is building, which is where we are building.
But we are trying to manage that we don't lose margin, maybe maximum we'll be compromising with 0.5 or we may be adding another 0.5 so it may depend upon the time.
We remain committed to open at least 90 to 100 new stores in the current financial year.

adds.what: New V-Mart/Unlimited stores: at least 90-100 stores in FY27 (38 opened in H1, about 40-42 more expected)
New office in Gurgaon and technology spend (part of H1 FY27 net capex)

growth.why: Management estimates FY27 total sales growth of 17-20% (midpoint ~18.5%), backed by 90-100 store openings (38 done in H1, ~40-42 more expected) and a targeted 5-6% price increase, though reported SSSG was only 3% and competitor openings are a headwind.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin flat at 33.5% vs 33.6%, EBITDA margin flat at 0.6% pre-Ind AS; management says margins can absorb about 0.5pp either way and still below 2017-19 levels, with Q3 V-Mart profitability expected strong but crude at $110-115 is a cost headwind.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 38 stores opened in H1 FY27 and about 40-42 more expected in H2 against a commitment of at least 90-100 FY27 openings, with net capex INR 85 crore in H1 already under way.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterates FY27 total sales growth of 17-20% backed by 40-42 more store openings and 5-6% price rise, though reported SSSG was only 3% and basket sizes are not growing much.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says bulk of cash flow will be redeployed into organic store and capacity expansion, with intent to focus new openings in South and West India; H1 net capex INR 85 crore vs INR 60 crore last year, though no utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated (not raised) 17-20% sales growth and called festive outlook positive but below internal targets, with reported SSSG at 3% versus 11% festival-adjusted.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Festive outlook below internal targets, October SSSG not disclosed, 150 competitor stores in target markets, and a further price increase may be needed in Q4 if crude stays at $110-115.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management credited new product lines and youth/kids wear at Unlimited for its SPSF turnaround (YTD SPSF INR 681, up 15%), and expects Q3 mix shift to higher ASP items, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: LimeRoad loss reduction
rows.why: LimeRoad losses fell to 8% of revenue from about 18% with top line up about 55%, and management is still pushing toward lower losses, though 8% of revenue is still a drag.

rows.label: Inventory days reduction
rows.why: Days of inventory fell to 90 from 97 and management expects further improvement as sales productivity grows, though short-term borrowings rose to INR 190 crore from INR 100 crore at March end.

rows.label: South and West India store push
rows.why: Unlimited EBITDA margin rose to 11.6% from 10.5% and YTD SPSF is up 15%, and management plans to focus new openings in South and West India.

tone.note: Management was confident on Unlimited and LimeRoad turnaround and on store openings, but cautious on consumer demand, input costs and competitor openings, and evasive on October SSSG and gross margin trajectory; analysts pushed on SSSG and margin recovery.
